amplify

/AM-pluh-fy/ - the stress falls on AM · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Amplify means to increase the strength or intensity of something.

Cupping his hands into a cone, the lifeguard amplified his shout enough to reach the swimmers at the far buoy.

Example

Two espressos before the recital didn't create Dana's stage fright — the fright was already there at breakfast. The caffeine amplified it, turning a flutter she could have played through into a tremor the whole front row could see in her bow hand.

Amplify is the precise verb because something that already existed was made stronger. The espressos invented nothing; they took an existing signal — her nerves — and turned it up. That is amplify's home ground: strengthening what is already present, whether a sound, a signal, or a feeling.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

augment: Augment means to make something larger by adding more to it — new lanes added to a highway, fresh voices added to a choir. Amplify adds nothing new; it takes what is already there and turns its strength up. Augmenting brings new material; amplifying strengthens the existing signal.

strengthen: Strengthen means to make something sturdier or more solid — a bridge, a friendship, an argument braced against attack. Amplify strengthens in one particular direction: it turns up the intensity of a sound, a signal, or a feeling so it registers more forcefully, not so it holds together better.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

muffle: wrap or smother a sound until it weakens

dampen: take the force or spirit out of something

Where it sits · how big the added push is

boost → amplify → supercharge

boost vs. amplify: A snack boosts your energy for an hour; amplify goes further, markedly strengthening a sound or feeling rather than giving it a small push.

supercharge vs. amplify: Supercharge sits past amplify on the dial: amplifying strengthens the engine's note, while supercharging forces the engine itself past its everyday limits.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ampl-: large, wide

Suffix — -ify: to make

Put it together: Ampl- (large, wide) + -ify (to make) = to make larger. Latin amplus meant 'wide, spacious'; amplificare meant to widen or enlarge. English bent the word toward strength: what you amplify — a current, a chorus, a worry — is made bigger in force, not in floor space.

Use the root in a new word: ample: The cabin's woodstove kept an ample stack of split logs drying beside it all winter.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Amplify strengthens what already exists — a sound, a signal, a feeling. Its unit-mates divide the work: intensify says the degree itself climbs (heat, pressure, a rivalry); magnify makes a thing merely look bigger or weightier than it is; inflate pushes a figure or claim past its true amount. Reach for amplify when something real gets turned up, most naturally a sound or an emotion.
